description.fun: Ralts reads the feelings of people and Pokémon with the red horns on its head: warm feelings warm its own body, while hostility sends it into hiding. It usually keeps out of sight, but it will come up to people when it senses happiness, and it prefers cheerful company to gloomy. A Ralts smiling in its sleep means something good happened that day.
description.guide: A small Psychic- and Fairy-type Pokémon (purely Psychic before Generation 6) that senses emotions with the horns on its head. It is shy but drawn to cheerful people. It evolves into Kirlia, which becomes Gardevoir or, if male, Gallade.
description.tagline: A shy empath that seeks out happy people

description.fun: Kirlia uses its hairpin-like horns to amplify its psychic power, warping the air into mirages and even glimpsing the future. It loves to dance on sunny mornings, grows more beautiful the happier its Trainer is, and even dances in its sleep, apparently dreaming of fun times ahead. Its name comes from Kirlian photography, said to capture psychic auras.
description.guide: A Psychic- and Fairy-type Pokémon (purely Psychic before Generation 6), the middle stage of the Ralts line, resembling a ballet dancer. It can see the future and loves to dance. It evolves into Gardevoir at level 30, or into Gallade if male and exposed to a Dawn Stone.
description.tagline: A ballet-dancing psychic that glimpses happy futures

branches.text: Kirlia becomes Gardevoir at level 30 whatever its gender, but a male Kirlia exposed to a Dawn Stone becomes Gallade instead. Gallade arrived in Generation 4, a generation after the rest of the family.

description.fun: Gardevoir will protect its Trainer with its life, and its power peaks when it does, letting it create small black holes and see the future. It can hold itself free of gravity, and it even sleeps upright, ready to protect people at any moment. Its name mixes the French for guard and duty, and its look combines a ballet dancer with a knight.
description.guide: A Psychic- and Fairy-type Pokémon (purely Psychic before Generation 6), one of Ralts's two final forms, with a gown-like body. It can see the future and will protect its Trainer with all its power. It can Mega Evolve into Mega Gardevoir, and the Paradox Pokémon Iron Valiant is said to be a future relative.
description.tagline: A devoted psychic guardian in a ballerina's gown

description.fun: Mega Gardevoir turns almost entirely white, its gown spreading wide like a bridal gown. The plate in its chest, said to be its heart made physical, splits open and unleashes tremendous psychic power.

Gallade is a master of courtesy and the sword: it extends blades from its elbows, sharper than any human-made sword, and reads its foe's moves to strike first. It senses when someone needs help and seeks them out, and it sleeps on one knee, ready to leap up and protect them. Its name blends gallant and blade.
description.guide: A Psychic- and Fighting-type Pokémon introduced in Generation 4, which a male Kirlia becomes when exposed to a Dawn Stone. It fights with blades that extend from its elbows and is protective of its Trainer. It can Mega Evolve into Mega Gallade.
description.tagline: A chivalrous psychic knight with blades on its elbows

description.fun: Mega Gallade's blades grow serrated plates that make them sharper still, and cape-like flaps sprout from its back for defence. When needed, it reshapes both arms into blades to fight two-handed, with a strength that comes from its bond with its Trainer.
